entities.summary:
Agasias of Ephesus (b. 50 BCE, Ephesus) was a renowned musician or composer of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Ephesus. He was known for his contributions to the fields of painters and sculptors.

Agasias was born in Ephesus, a city in ancient Anatolia, and spent his life mastering the art of music. His work had a profound impact on the development of classical music, and he is often credited as one of the most influential musicians of his time.

Agasias' legacy extends beyond his own work, as his compositions influenced generations of musicians to come. His music continues to be studied and performed today, providing a glimpse into the cultural and artistic achievements of ancient Greece.

Agasias of Ephesus is a testament to the enduring power of art and music to shape our understanding of the world and ourselves. His contributions to the classical music canon remain an important part of our shared cultural heritage.
